question.text: An AIF chooses to structure as an LLP. Which of the following is a consequence?

answer.text: Entry and exit of partners (investors) becomes a cumbersome process under the partnership deed
The fund enjoys better tax treatment than a trust
The fund can have unlimited investors without any limit

explanation.text: The Logic: In an LLP AIF, every investor becomes a partner; entry and exit are cumbersome under the partnership deed, and investor details enter the public domain via MCA regulation (pp. 103, 189-190). The Trap: LLPs do not offer better tax treatment than trusts for AIFs in India. Confidentiality is also lower, since partner details are publicly filed. Note: Detailed step-by-step exit-process comparisons (deed amendments, MCA filing timelines, comparisons to unit-transfer speed) are not directly sourced in the cited pages and should be separately verified before being relied upon.
